evidence: 实测 loopback CPU / calibrated 模拟
hardware_device: Apple M4 Max / CPU / 1 native thread
measurement_unit: whole round including arrival window and drain

semantics.arrival: Seeded T3 Poisson arrivals and lengths replayed identically across C/Q and rounds; token IDs use a separate seeded RNG. Open loop: full C-slot client pool drops arrivals immediately, without a hidden executor queue or retries.
semantics.avalanche: T3 unchanged: p99 > threshold OR four strictly increasing final-half-window time-weighted queue means, slope > min_slope_per_s, horizon queue >= min_queue. Evaluate each round separately; report triggering repeat count.
semantics.connection_pool: C prestarted HTTP client threads, at most C live sockets. Server sends Connection: close, so each call opens a fresh socket; no keepalive reuse.
semantics.limits: Single process serial CPU inference, loopback, no TLS, local client threads compete with server. Fixed seed does not fix OS timing/admission. Not production capacity or proof of divergence.
semantics.measurement: P0 measure() times whole rounds with tracemalloc; warmup excluded. Successful request E2E includes dispatch lag; wire_ms starts inside client thread. Quantiles use NumPy linear; timeouts and 429 are separate, never zero-latency successes.
semantics.queue: Sample actual service.queue.qsize() at queue_sample_ms; integrate piecewise-constant samples. This is a sampled finite-window proxy with observed sampling gaps, not an exact event trace.
semantics.simulation: P1-T4 calibrated T3 service model, static batch_size=1 and batch_timeout_ms=0. Serial FIFO adapter adds the same C client cap and immediate client-full drops, Q excludes active inference. Ideal zero HTTP transport/rejection cost, no socket failures; client timeout represented at response deadline while inference drains. Unbounded-client adapter verified against T3.
semantics.throughput: Successful full responses received by horizon / arrival window seconds; drained successful requests / max(horizon,last response) separately. No token/s comparison: HTTP whole endpoint exposes no token timestamps.
